subject: Position Announcement: Visiting Assistant Professor in Behavioral Science, Environmental and Water Resources (Delaware State University)
title: Position Announcement: Visiting Assistant Professor in Behavioral Science, Environmental and Water Resources (Delaware State University)
text:
---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: Leah H. Palm-Forster via CWAE <cwae@aaealist.org>
Date: Mon, Aug 24, 2026 at 7:34 AM
Subject: [AAEA CWAE] Position Announcement: Visiting Assistant Professor in Behavioral Science, Environmental and Water Resources (Delaware State University)
To: Leah Palm-Forster <leahhp@udel.edu>

Dear Colleagues,
 
We want to highlight a new opportunity at Delaware State University that may be of interest to your students, postdocs, and colleagues. DSU's College of Agriculture, Science and Technology is hiring a Visiting Assistant Professor in Behavioral Science related to Environmental and Water Resources. This position is funded by the National Science Foundation and is a twelve-month faculty appointment based in Dover, Delaware, with 75 percent of effort devoted to research and 25 percent to teaching, student engagement, and experiential learning.
 
The position centers on human behavioral responses to water resource challenges, with particular attention to saltwater intrusion risk and coastal resilience. The successful candidate will design and conduct field and laboratory experiments, develop and implement surveys on public decision making around water management and climate adaptation, and work with interdisciplinary teams studying the biophysical, social, and economic drivers of saltwater intrusion. The role includes collaboration with the University of Delaware's Center for Experimental and Applied Economics and other partner institutions, access to an experimental economics lab, and opportunities to mentor undergraduate and graduate students, co-author peer-reviewed publications, and contribute to policy-relevant research on climate adaptation.
 
A Ph.D. in behavioral science, applied economics, psychology, sociology, or a closely related field with an emphasis on human decision making and behavior is required, along with demonstrated coursework in research methodology, particularly experimental economics, survey research, or related experimental methods.
 
Here’s a link to the full description on the Delaware State University website: https://www.schooljobs.com/careers/desu/jobs/5434146/visiting-assistant-professor-in-behavioral-science-related-to-environmental-and-w .  We are happy to talk about the position, and you can learn more about the hiring process and Delaware State University by contacting the search chair, Dr. Gulni Ozbay (gozbay@desu.edu).
  
Best regards,
Kent Messer & Leah Palm-Forster

subject: Early career research participation opportunity with USGS
title: Early career research participation opportunity with USGS
text:
Please share this announcement widely:

Early career research participation opportunity

Position summary: The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) Fort Collins Science Center is seeking one or more students or recent graduates to participate in applied research projects conducted by the Social and Economic Analysis
 branch (https://www.usgs.gov/centers/fort-collins-science-center/science/social-and-economic-analysis-research-support-public).
 Selected candidates will be provided with important research and training opportunities, joining existing collaborations among USGS scientists and resource managers, scientists from other agencies within the Department of the Interior, and other student services
 contractors.

The immediate focus of this position will be working with a team to inform management of water-based recreation and natural resources in the Colorado River Basin, with an emphasis on Glen Canyon National Recreation Area, Grand Canyon National Park, and Lake
 Mead National Recreation Area. The position will entail participating in economic research, for example compiling and analyzing visitation and recreation data, conducting nonmarket valuation analysis and other statistical modeling, synthesizing qualitative
 and quantitative information from multiple sources, interpreting results, and drafting and publishing research findings, all while working closely with staff from USGS and partner agencies. Research activities may include evaluating how drought-related changes
 in reservoir levels, river flows, and dam operations influence recreational access, visitation, recreation quality, and associated economic benefits under alternative water management scenarios.

Qualifications: To be eligible for consideration, candidates must have completed an MS degree or higher in economics, social science, data science, natural resources management, or a related field. Candidates must either be currently enrolled at a college
 or university or have completed their latest graduate degree within the last 12 months. Applicants must be U.S. citizens and undergo a background check.

Candidates must have demonstrated experience implementing economics research. Experience with quantitative data analysis is required, including but not limited to analyzing and modeling survey, spatial, or other data in open-source coding platforms (e.g., Program
 R, Python). Experience with contributing to peer-reviewed publications is strongly desired.

Applicants must demonstrate excellent written and oral communication skills. Familiarity with public lands or water management or the management of recreation on public lands is desired. Applicants should also possess strong collaboration and time-management
 skills.

The position will be hired as a student services contractor with an initial contract for part-time during spring 2027 and full-time through summer 2027. Remote work is possible. Student services contractors participate in
 scientific research projects at USGS Science Centers across the U.S. and work directly with USGS scientists to gain hands-on experience in real-world science projects, build technical and professional skills, explore potential science careers and pathways,
 and receive mentorship from experienced scientists (https://www.usgs.gov/youth-and-education-in-science/student-services-contractors).
 Candidates will need to have an active SAMS account (System for Award Management, sam.gov) prior to appointment; more information will be provided upon selection.

How to apply:  Applicants should submit (1) a cover letter describing their experience, qualifications, and interest in the position, (2) a CV (or resume) (with the month and year for degrees received/anticipated clearly
 listed), (3) a primary-authored writing sample, (4) undergraduate and graduate transcripts (unofficial is fine) showing completion of their most recent degree, and (5) contact information for three professional references. Materials should be submitted to
 James Meldrum (jmeldrum@usgs.gov)
 in PDF format (multiple files ok); please use "CoRRec SSC opportunity application" in the subject line. For full consideration, submit applications by the end of
Sunday, November 8, 2026.

Thank you, 

James

subject: Research/Business Analyst position at Southwick Associates
title: Research/Business Analyst position at Southwick Associates
text:
Hello colleagues,

Southwick Associates is expanding its team and looking for someone with at least two years of experience conducting quantitative survey and statistical based analysis. 
 Please feel free to forward the job description (below and attached) to anyone you think may be interested and/or reach out to me with questions.

 

All the best,

Lisa

Research/Business Analyst

Southwick Associates is a market research, economics and statistics consulting firm specializing in serving the outdoor equipment industry, state fish and wildlife agencies, conservation and sportsmen’s NGOs, and supporting businesses. Celebrating more
 than 35 years, we are known as problem-solvers, developing solutions and new products now widely used by our client base. We are the go-to firm in the natural resources and traditional outdoor recreation fields when challenges surface and difficult-to-find
 insights are needed. Our staff, located across the U.S., work in a collaborative, flexible environment that allows us to take our clients to new levels of success. 

Position: Full-time Research/Business Analyst for hunting, fishing, target shooting, outdoor recreation, and natural resources consulting.

Responsibilities: This role is ideal for an early-career professional who enjoys working with data, conducting research, identifying trends, and supporting business decision-making. The analyst will assist in gathering, analyzing, and interpreting information
 from multiple sources to help drive operational, strategic, and client-focused initiatives. The professional in this position will conduct quantitative surveys and statistical-based analyses. They will also be someone who can go beyond summarizing the data
 in front of them to better support clients’ needs with substantive insights. As a representative of Southwick Associates, strong communication skills are a must. Occasional travel
will be required. This professional will join a skilled and experienced team. Analysts work independently or collaboratively, depending on the client’s needs.

Qualifications:

Bachelor’s or master’s degree in a quantitative field such as statistics, economics, or business analytics is required. Two or more years of related work experience is preferred. Strong analytical skills in the areas of primary and secondary research are required.

Experience with supporting the design, management, and execution of research projects that include data collection, analysis, and reporting (technical report, infographic, or presentations).

Proficiency with R statistical software and MS Office suite is required. Additional beneficial proficiencies include SPSS, Stata, and other similar programs, as well as online survey platforms.

Independent self-starter, organized, self-disciplined, and able to work individually or as part of a team with limited oversight.

Strong organizational, written, and oral communication skills are a must. Examples of written work are requested.

Detail-oriented with a commitment to accuracy, quality, and meeting or exceeding deadlines.

Hunting, target shooting, or fishing experience is preferred.

All staff work remotely from locations of their choosing all across the U.S. Experience working in this kind of environment is also preferred.  

Compensation:

Starting salary of $68,000–$74,000 depending on experience, plus an annual profit-sharing bonus. Benefits include a 401(k) with 4% company match; access to medical, dental, and vision coverage; and generous paid time off: 12 vacation days per year in the first
 two years (increasing with tenure), 14 paid holidays, sick leave, and parental leave.  

Posting closes on December 1, 2026 or once filled. Send cover letter, resume, and writing/communications experience to
LBragg@SouthwickAssociates.com. 

 

Lisa Bragg | VP Operations

Mobile (207) 852-1149 • Office (720) 686 3527

Southwick Associates •
  PO Box 470580 • Aurora, CO 80047

subject: open rank faculty position and director of the Northeast Extension Risk Management Education Center
title: open rank faculty position and director of the Northeast Extension Risk Management Education Center
text:
Dear CWAE Colleagues, 

I'm delighted to share that our department is hiring a new faculty member in ag economics (open rank) who will also serve as the director of the Northeast Extension Risk Management Education Center (NERME) in the College of Agriculture and Natural Resources at the University of Delaware. Position details are copied below.

Please reach out to our search committee chair, Dr. Michelle Segovia (segoviam@udel.edu), with any questions. You're also welcome to reach out to me. 

Kind regards,
Leah

Leah H. Palm-Forster, Ph.D.
Professor and Associate Chair, Applied Economics & Statistics
Director, Center for Experimental & Applied Economics
University of Delaware  

531 S College Ave. Newark, DE 19716
(302) 831-1325 

Faculty webpage
leahhp@udel.edu

Open Rank Professor of Agricultural Economics and Director of the Northeast Extension Risk Management Education Center (NERME), College of Agriculture and Natural Resources

POSITION:
The Department of Applied Economics and Statistics seeks a full-time, open rank, tenure-track or tenured faculty member in applied economics with an emphasis in agricultural economics, beginning in Fall 2027. The successful candidate’s research program will engage with risk management, broadly construed. The successful candidate will also serve as Director of the Northeast Extension Risk Management Education Center (NERME), housed at the University of Delaware. The position combines leadership of a regional extension center with an active research program, extension research and programming in partnership with UD Cooperative Extension, and undergraduate teaching in the Food and Agribusiness Marketing program. The position will be a 9-month, academic-year appointment at the rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor with 40% of time devoted to research, 35% to teaching, and 25% to service and administration. Rank and tenure status will be commensurate with qualifications and experience.

REQUIREMENTS: 
Ph.D. in agricultural economics, applied economics, economics, agribusiness, or a closely related field. The successful candidate is expected to have demonstrated excellence in research, commensurate with rank, a clear interest in high-quality extension, outreach and teaching activities, and the organizational and communication skills needed to lead a multi-state, grant-funded program. They should be adept at engaging a broad range of students, producers, and stakeholders through their research, teaching, outreach, and mentoring.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:
Experience writing and managing competitive grants, particularly federal awards such as those from USDA National Institute of Food and Agriculture (NIFA); experience administering programs, budgets, or sub-awards; experience designing or delivering extension or outreach programs for agricultural producers, agribusinesses, or other food system stakeholders; experience working with Cooperative Extension partners across institutions or states; and a research record or clearly articulated research agenda in agricultural, food, and natural resource risk management, broadly construed.

There is a strong desire for candidates who will serve the full range of Delaware and Northeast agricultural producers, agribusinesses, food system stakeholders, students, and communities through their research, teaching, outreach, and mentoring.

GENERAL INFORMATION:
The Department of Applied Economics and Statistics is an interdisciplinary academic unit within the University of Delaware's College of Agriculture and Natural Resources. Currently, the Department consists of 19 faculty who teach and supervise approximately 100 undergraduate majors and 80 graduate students. The Department includes the Center for Experimental & Applied Economics, a large experimental economics laboratory, a statistical lab, and the Northeast Extension Risk Management Education Center (NERME), a regional center funded through the USDA-NIFA Extension Risk Management Education program that supports risk management education for agricultural producers across the Northeast. Recognized as one of America's best universities to work for, the University of Delaware is in Newark, Delaware, within two hours of New York, Philadelphia, Baltimore, and Washington, D.C.  The University is a Land Grant, Sea Grant, Space Grant, and Carnegie Research University.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Director of NERME
The successful candidate will serve as Director of NERME and provide leadership and strategic vision for the Center. Responsibilities include preparing and submitting the Center’s annual grant proposals; overseeing the Center’s competitive sub-award system, including requests for applications, proposal review, award management, and reporting of project results; and managing the Center’s budget and staff. The Director is expected to think strategically about the direction of NERME, to secure and strengthen its place at the University of Delaware within the College of Agriculture and Natural Resources and the Department of Applied Economics and Statistics, and to build connections between NERME, UD Cooperative Extension, and faculty research across the University and the Northeast region. The Director is expected to develop and maintain a collaborative relationship with the other regional ERME Centers and the Digital ERME Center to support the mission of the USDA-NIFA funded program.

Research
The successful candidate is expected to establish or continue an active, externally funded research program in agricultural economics with national and international visibility, with a focus on risk management, broadly construed. Relevant areas include, but are not limited to, market and production risk, agricultural and food policy, conservation and natural resource management, and behavioral and experimental approaches to decision-making under risk. We especially welcome research that complements the department’s strengths in experimental and behavioral economics applied to agricultural policy and consumer decision-making. The extension research component of the appointment should connect the candidate’s research program to NERME’s mission and to the needs of producers, agribusinesses, and food system stakeholders in Delaware and the Northeast. Collaboration with other faculty and/or professionals in related fields is strongly encouraged. At least one element of the candidate’s research program should contribute to the College’s local, regional, and/or national research priorities. This position will contribute to the University and College’s strategic visions through excellence in graduate education, innovative partnerships, community and industry engagement, and world-class research efforts.

Extension
The successful candidate will conduct extension research and programming that supports UD Cooperative Extension activities related to risk management for agricultural and food businesses. They will work cooperatively with Extension colleagues to design and participate in workshops, decision tools, publications, and other communications that help Delaware and Northeast farmers, agribusinesses, and food system stakeholders manage risk and make sound decisions in an ever-changing market and policy environment. They will participate in cooperative grant solicitations to support the work of UD Cooperative Extension, and are expected to draw on NERME’s regional network to extend the reach of UD programming.

Teaching
Yearly workload consists of two undergraduate courses for the Food and Agribusiness Marketing program or related areas. Candidates will have the opportunity to contribute to the undergraduate and graduate programs through advising and mentoring, as well as directing theses and research projects.

SALARY
University of Delaware salaries and fringe benefit packages compete favorably with other universities in general and land grant universities in particular. A start-up package will be available.

CONTACT
For more information,

institution: University of Victoria on Economics of Carbon Storage
text:

Subject: Post-Doc Position at University of Victoria on Economics of Carbon Storage
To: <CLIMATEECONOMETRICS@jiscmail.ac.uk>

Dear Colleagues,

We’re hiring a postdoc on the Economics of Geological Carbon Storage at the University of Victoria, on Vancouver Island.

The position is part of Solid Carbon (https://solidcarbon.ca/), a project run by UVic and Ocean Networks Canada on storing CO2 permanently as rock in the basalt beneath the seafloor off the island. The research covers storage
 costs and how these might evolve, whether scaling up is feasible, and how policy (carbon pricing, carbon takeback obligations and other instruments) interacts with CO2 storage. There will also be protected time for the candidate's own research.

The post is for 3 years and starts in summer 2027. We welcome applicants with a PhD in economics, agricultural and resource economics, environmental science, geography or a related field who have strong quantitative and empirical skills.

Review of applications begins January 15, 2027.

Apply via EconJobMarket: https://econjobmarket.org/positions/12852

Please share with anyone who might be interested!

Best,

Felix

subject: Post-doctoral position in the economics and policy of critical minerals
title: Post-doctoral position in the economics and policy of critical minerals
text:
Hi all,

 

I am recruiting a post-doctoral associate in the Baker School of Public Policy at the University of Tennessee to work on the
economics and policy of critical minerals.  The successful candidate will work with me, Dr. Georg Schaur, and Dr. Tim Fitzgerald to develop a research agenda in one or both of the following areas:

Costs of US critical mineral dependence on foreign countries
Effects of industrial policy on investment in critical mineral mining, processing, and recycling

The position is a good fit for candidates with interest in international trade, industrial organization, risk and uncertainty, energy, and natural resources.  The successful candidate will have the opportunity
 to work closely with colleagues at UTK, Oak Ridge National Lab, and critical mineral industry partners. The position is for 2 years starting in summer/fall 2027 (exact start date negotiable).

subject: Position Search: UMaine Dean of the College of Earth, Life, and Health Sciences
title: Position Search: UMaine Dean of the College of Earth, Life, and Health Sciences
text:
Dear Colleagues,

I wanted to share that the University fo Maine has just launched a national search for our next Dean of the College of Earth, Life, and Health Sciences (ELH), which is the home of UMaine's School of Economics, School of Forest Resources, and School of Food and Agriculture.

The Dean of ELH will join the University of Maine at a pivotal moment in the institution's history. As Maine's flagship public university and the state's only land, sea, and space grant institution, UMaine combines the strengths of a Carnegie R1 research university with an unwavering commitment to public service, innovation, and economic development. Located in Orono and serving approximately 10,600 students, UMaine is recognized internationally for leadership in climate science, forestry, marine sciences, advanced materials, and sustainable ecosystems. From its forests, farms, laboratories, research centers, and coastal facilities to partnerships across the state, the university serves as a living laboratory where discovery directly enhances the environmental, economic, and social well-being of Maine and beyond.

The anticipated salary range for the position is $250,000 to $275,000. The final compensation package will be commensurate with experience, qualifications, and leadership accomplishments.

More details on the position can be found on the UMS Jobs website and WittKeifer website.

Cheers,
Adam
